DETAILED INSTALLMENT ABSTRACTS, 1-CALL BRIEFS & LOSSLESS PART LINKS (§01–§09)

Executive Summaries & Direct Links for All Nine Articles

  • §01 — An AI Output Is Not an Act: The Lawful-Act Defect and Machine Standing: Problem: Valid JSON, credentials, confidence, and a green tool result can make an AI proposal look authorized when it is not. Proves: Machine standing binds the exact act, actor, evidence, target, execution, time, and terminal disposition before consequence. Routes: /01/brief/ · /01/brief.txt · /01.md · P1 P2 P3 P4 P5 P6
  • §02 — Zero-Trust Document Ingestion and Server-Cut Evidence: Problem: Hostile documents can attack the parser, while models can fabricate citations and make unknown coverage disappear. Proves: LPAC parser confinement, immutable views, explicit omissions, and server-cut srv_ and ev_ receipts establish served evidence. Routes: /02/brief/ · /02/brief.txt · /02.md · P1 P2 P3 P4
  • §03 — EISA Four-Gate Verdict Machine & Strict AST Parser: Problem: Entity resolution needs rich comparison structure, but raw contacts, companies, and products should not be sent to external AI providers. Proves: The production EISA Four-Gate machine validates bounded acts over sealed evidence; Semantic Switch is an experimental alpha structure-preservation research module. Routes: /03/brief/ · /03/brief.txt · /03.md · P1 P2 P3 P4 P5 P6
  • §04 — The Room: Why Git and Chat Are Not Coordination Planes: Problem: Git history and chat transcripts cannot establish who may act, receive, stop, or complete work now. Proves: The Room revalidates territory, causal observation, sealed wakes, native replies, cancellation, and privileged acceptance. Routes: /04/brief/ · /04/brief.txt · /04.md · P1 P2 P3 P4 P5
  • §05 — Expiry Is Not Fencing: Typed Leases and Kernel Write Exclusion: Problem: An expired lease does not physically stop a stale worker or an uncooperative local writer from changing a resource. Proves: Monotonic generations, current tenancy, typed scopes, and overlapping Win32 handle exclusion fence the write itself. Routes: /05/brief/ · /05/brief.txt · /05.md · P1 P2 P3 P4
  • §06 — Rollback Is Not Erasure: Dual-Tier Vaults and Ungated Quarantine: Problem: A single undo snapshot can destroy intermediate states and launder unauthorized writes into a clean baseline. Proves: Primary certifies operational recovery while Amber preserves every intermediate and ungated state for forensics. Routes: /06/brief/ · /06/brief.txt · /06.md · P1 P2 P3
  • §07 — Defeating Approval Laundering: Act Pinning and Successor Grants: Problem: Approval for action A can become a different action A′ at execution, and a crash can separate commit from receipt. Proves: Pre-resume confinement, controller-fixed RequestedAct, fenced SQLite, and non-fabricating successor grants preserve act and return continuity. Routes: /07/brief/ · /07/brief.txt · /07.md · P1 P2 P3
  • §08 — The Sovereign Kill Switch: Break-Glass Epochs and the Conformance Gate: Problem: A kill switch the agent can clear is not a boundary, and a green build does not prove the release enforces refusals. Proves: Latch-first containment, scoped epochs, observed Job termination, in-doubt recovery, and the 45-case candidate gate close the loop. Routes: /08/brief/ · /08/brief.txt · /08.md · P1 P2 P3 P4
  • §09 — Bring One Real Boundary: Technical Peer Review, Challenge Tracks & R&D Evaluation: Problem: Writing code by hand is no longer the bottleneck. The bottleneck is formalizing the trust boundary, decomposing work across parallel AI agents without context collapse, catching plausible-but-wrong outputs, and proving that invalid transitions fail closed. Proves: AINA is both a deterministic execution-governance runtime (squad.exe) and Exhibit A of a repeatable 9-IDE multi-agent engineering methodology grounded in 11+ years of production systems delivery. Routes: /09/brief/ · /09/brief.txt · /09.md · P1 P2 P3 P4 P5 P6 P7 P8
